SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT
Section 1, Special Br. C 84/30.
File No.
Date March 24, 1930.

Subject (in full) Labour Unions in Eastern District.

Made by. C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang. Forwarded by J Boyne D S I

I beg to forward herewith a tabulated list of labour
unions in the Eastern District. In all there are at present
12 unions in that area. Of this number three are subject to
the control of the Seamen's General Labour Union and the remain-
ing nine to the General Labour Union and the local tangpu.
These unions are so far unknown to have any connections with
the Chung Nyi Association or the Chinese Communist Party.
With the exception of the three unions under the control
of the Seamen's General Labour Union, Chow Hsueh-siang (周学湘),
a Standing Committee Member of the General Labour Union, exercises
considerable influence over the labour unions in the Eastern
District especially the 4th District Cigarette Factory Workers'
Union, of which he is the Chairman. It is worthy of note that
Chow Hsueh-siang is a close follower of Chu Hsueh Fan (朱学范), a
responsible member of the General Labour Union, and Loh Ching-ds
(陸京士), a prominent member of the local Tangpu, both of whom
are very influential among the local labour circles.

P.A.
Useful. Keep up to date
Sih Tse-liang
C. D. I.
J.B. 25/3
D.C. (Special Branch). Western District Office
S.I. M/C Trans to Reg. 8.612.243

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
报告
第一部分，特别处 C 84/30。
档案号。
日期：1930年3月24日。

主题（全称）：东区工会。

呈报人：刑事侦缉探员 施子良 (Sih Tse-liang)。转呈人：副督察长 J Boyne

兹随函附上东区工会一览表。目前该地区共有工会12个。其中三个受海员总工会控制，其余九个受总工会及当地党部控制。截至目前，这些工会与忠义协会或中国共产党没有任何关联。

除受海员总工会控制的三个工会外，总工会常务委员周学湘 (Chow Hsueh-siang) 对东区的工会，特别是他担任主席的第四区卷烟厂工人公会，具有相当大的影响力。值得注意的是，周学湘是总工会负责人朱学范 (Chu Hsueh Fan) 以及当地党部重要成员陆京士 (Loh Ching-ds) 的亲信追随者，这两人在当地劳工界均极具影响力。

P.A.
有用。保持更新
施子良
刑事侦缉探员
J.B. 3月25日

In accordance with instructions from D.C. (Special Branch)
I beg to forward herewith a tabulated list of labour unions
in the Western District. In all there are at present eight
unions in that area. Of this number five are subject to the
control of the General Labour Union and the Chinese authorities;
and two, which were formed by the followers of the Chung Nyi
Association, are almost inactive at present, but are likely to
resume their activities when opportunity arises. These seven
unions are so far not known to have any connections with the
Communist Party.
The remaining one is an organization of unemployed cotton
mill workers, sponsored by pro-communistic elements, who are
endeavouring to gain influence over the unemployed, but up to
the present its success has been negligible.

Sih Tse Liang
